summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to Rs 235 crore, but EBITDA fell to Rs 72 crore (31% margin) on heavy opex, with management guiding 35-40% margins from Q3.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was about Rs 235 crore in Q2 FY27, up 24% YoY and 5% QoQ, with gross margin steady near 88%. EBITDA was about Rs 72 crore at a 31% margin, down from 48% a year earlier and 41% in Q1, as operating expenses rose sharply on advertising, staff, new centres and technology. Management attributed the miss to a pricing and mix shift toward cheaper daycare and small packages, a lapse in government business during the payment delay, camp timing errors, and a push into e-commerce products that carry lower margins. H1 FY27 revenue was about Rs 460 crore (up 26% YoY) with EBITDA of about Rs 164 crore (36% margin). Management reiterated 35-40% margins, 20-25% growth and 3,900 beds by January, but the call was defensive and several answers were unclear.

segments.name: Hospital / Panchkarma services
segments.commentary: Management said IPD volumes fell about 45% QoQ as the company shifted patients to daycare with 2-day stays. IPD was about 11,500 in Q1 and daycare about 19,000, with the company citing a rise in Q2 daycare numbers. Ticket size fell after rate cuts and small packages for BP, sugar, thyroid and joint pain.

segments.name: E-commerce / OTC products
segments.commentary: Management said it shut 4-6 product experiments in November and kept a core set of about 10 products (including Dr Maa Dr Paa, Vitamin C buckthorn and gut care) with ROAS of 6-7x. E-commerce monthly sales were cited at about Rs 25-29 crore recently. Management said OTC and Ayurveda shop-model plans were cancelled because of low profit.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guided at 35-40% from Q3 FY27 onwards; management said Q3 would be challenging with Diwali disruption and a further Rs 20-24 crore of incremental other expenses per quarter, falling to about Rs 20-21 crore after Q3.

Management said 20-25% growth is achievable, and said FY27 revenue of Rs 1,000 crore would need about Rs 90-95 crore monthly sales in the remaining four months. Management said the Rs 250-300 crore figure is hard this year, with the 250 crore figure given as the target to be met, and said Q4 would show the trajectory.
Operational beds expected at about 3,900 by end-January 2027, with Lucknow and Ahmedabad hospitals (150 beds each) and a new small hospital starting in January.
Government (CGHS, CAPS, ECHS) business to be restarted under portal 2.0; management capped government share at about 15% of business and expects payments to flow within 2-6 months.
Management said it is considering a share buyback, to be discussed at a board meeting that week, after consultation with the management team and major shareholders.
Management said Manali resort pilot and VVIP wellness centre would start on 15 December, with machines delayed by the Iran-Iraq war, and it expects 15-20 rooms a day to generate Rs 8-10 crore profit.
capex_capacity: Target of 3,900 operational beds by end-January 2027 (from current base); Lucknow and Ahmedabad each to start with 150 beds in January.

Plans to announce 4-6 new hospitals in South India, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Bengal and Tamil Nadu in the next 2-4 months, including government-linked empanelment; existing hospitals in Chennai, Hyderabad and Bangalore described as small.
Call centre of 300 seats set up in Navi Mumbai, expected to start contributing in January-February 2027.
Chandigarh research infrastructure established; company said it had hired retired NCISM head as research consultant.
Manali VVIP wellness resort on a lease model (108 rooms, 26 villas) with a soft launch and paid operations from 15 December; hyperbaric oxygen and ozone machines delayed.
demand_pricing: Management said ticket size fell after rate cuts for Ayushman card holders and preventive packages, with some small-hospital rates halved. The company said it expects ticket size to recover over the next 2-4 quarters.

Camp-based business in the Mayurbhanj-type camp model (named as 'mayorate camp' on the call) fell in September due to wrong camp timing and a lost main doctor; management said new doctors from a large cancer hospital were onboarded for October.
Government business fell after payment delays; management said portal 2.0 has restarted and payments are expected to arrive on time, with the company capping government share at 15%.
Daycare growth is driven by health insurers now paying for daycare; management said small-hospital packages for diabetes, BP, lung and joint pain will have 2-day admissions with rest as daycare.
Management said acquisition cost in e-commerce is high; peers such as Kapiva and Gaia Veda were cited as loss-making on that basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall and what is the outlook for Q3 and FY27 EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a lower ticket size from the Ayushman-linked rate cuts, Diwali disruption, and e-commerce-led spending. It guided to 35-40% EBITDA margin from Q3 and said the incremental other expenses would fall after Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company reach 3,000 operational beds by end-2026 and what is the Q3 margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3,900 beds would be operational by end-January 2027, with a focus on occupancy and a 35-40% margin in the coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the large increase in other expenses and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the increase to lease rentals, e-commerce costs, courier, development and travel, plus a Rs 3.1 crore fair value loss, with the analyst's calculation of incremental expense about Rs 46 crore YoY. Management said it would reduce the incremental spend by about 50% in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Has the decision to cancel OTC and shop models been made, and what is the revised strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said OTC and shop-based models were cancelled due to low margin and high cost. It is focusing on e-commerce for direct-to-consumer sales and daycare-led hospital growth, with details to follow in the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company do a buyback or consider a strategic investor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a board meeting that week would consider a buyback, after consulting its management and major shareholders. It also mentioned a possible strategic investor.

risks_watch: Margin recovery to 35-40% from Q3 depends on controlling other expenses, which management itself said would be about Rs 20-24 crore per quarter, while Q2 margin was 31%.
Government receivables: portal 2.0 restart and payment timing are unproven; management said it would cap government share at 15%.
IPD volume fell sharply and ticket size fell; a shift to daycare reduces revenue per patient.
Management's FY27 Rs 1,000 crore revenue (or Rs 250-300 crore EBITDA) goals look hard, and guidance was described inconsistently on the call.

Governance and disclosure: several figures (e.g., beds, opex, other expense, occupancy) were inconsistent; the Q2 result drew a shareholder complaint over lack of upfront disclosure of the expense rise.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term vision and new models, but defensive and evasive on the Q2 shortfall, expense detail and FY27 targets. Management repeatedly blamed Diwali, camp timing and a lapse in government payments, and several answers were incomplete or hard to follow.
